To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
polar solvation and the configurational entropy are important for the potency of antiretrovirals against HIV-1 proteases.
polar solvation free and configurational entropy contribute significantly to binding affinity changes and drug resistance.

(1) drug resistance is mainly due to unfavorable shifts in van-der-Waals interactions and configuratonal entropy, (2) the polar solvation energy is important for the affinity of HIV-1 PR and (3) configurational entropy is important for relative binding affinites of HIV-1 inhibitors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of drugs that are potent against HIV-1 proteases that are resistant against the currently available drugs and the molecular forces that govern drug resistance.
the rational drug design of antiretorviral drugs targeting the HIV-1 proteas.
a better understanding of the molecular basis of the potency of antiretrovirals targeting HIV-1 PR and how mutations affect binding affinities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the binding of both KNI-10133 and KNI 10175 is driven by favorable van der Waals and electrostatic interactions and favorable polar and nonpolar solvation free energy contributions, but unfavorable configurational entropy changes.

the binding affinity for a particular inhibitor is governed by a complex combination of favorable and unfavorable intermolecular interactions as well as unfavorable changes in polar solvation and entropy.
the polar component of the solvated free energy is important for the binding affinity and that configurational entropy must be taken into consideration in the computation of binding affinites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding free energies of the inhibitors KNI-10073 and KNI-10575 to wild-type HIV-1 proteases are mainly governed by the nonpolar solvation free energy.
polar solvation free energetics and configurational entropy must be taken into consideration in the design of HIV-1 PR drugs.
both polar solvation and changes in configurational entropies are important for the design of antireviral drugs targeting the HIV-1 PR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding affinities of KNI-10175 and KNI-10133 for the wild-type HIV-1 proteases are similar and comparable to darunavir.
the polar component of the solvational free energy is a key factor in the design of antiretoviral drugs against HIV-1 proteases.

the polar solvation and the configurational entropy must be considered in the computation of binding free energies and that neglecting them may lead to erroneous conclusions about the origin of binding affinity or mutation-induced affinity change.
